body:
## Module 5 in two minutes

> ⚠️ **Counsel review required before deployment.** Every specific here moves. One of them moved nine days before this was written.

**You own the trust deficit whether or not you owned the design decision.** Accountability without authority, which is a genuinely bad structural position and the honest starting point.

**The asymmetry, in numbers** `[V]`: only **26%** of candidates trust AI to evaluate them fairly (Gartner, n=2,918), ~79% want to be told when it is used, and **~38% have walked away from a process that included an AI interview**: behavioural, not attitudinal. Meanwhile HR has no direct involvement in AI strategy in **52%** of organizations. The systems spending that trust are chosen by people who don't carry the consequence.

**Deferral is not runway** `[V]`. EU high-risk employment duties moved to 2 December 2027, but AI literacy and the **absolute** emotion-recognition prohibition have bound since February 2025, and transparency obligations since 2 August 2026 — a recruiting or HR chatbot is in scope now.

## The durable rule

**AI is never the decision-maker. Automate the assembly, not the reasoning.**

A system may gather, structure, summarize, rank for review, and flag. **A person decides, and that person is nameable.** Statutory positions have moved twice in eighteen months in both directions, a posture built on a date expires, and this one is stricter than most current law, which is exactly what makes it durable.

And: **the difference between a policy and governance is whether anything has ever been refused.**

## What the full module adds

Why the emotion-recognition prohibition matters to *this* function specifically, engagement inference from webcam is marketed here. The policy arithmetic: roughly 49% have a policy and about a quarter of those believe it is clear and durable, so **around one organization in eight has one its own people think will hold** `[V]`. The one-minute diagnostic — *when did your organization last say no to an AI deployment, and who was told?* **The disclosure scenario** that no policy addresses: an employee confides in a coaching tool for six weeks, it never escalates, she resigns and alleges the company knew. Every position is uncomfortable; the failure is that nobody chose, so the vendor's default decides. Ten systems to sort. And the activity: go and find one.
